input:
The pump affinity laws give the performance of a centrifugal pump at a changed speed from its performance at a known speed, for the same pump handling the same liquid. The laws are three proportionalities. Flow is proportional to speed: at double the speed, the pump delivers double the flow. Head is proportional to the square of the speed. Power is proportional to the cube of the speed. The three proportionalities hold together, so a speed change large enough to matter for flow has a larger effect on the head and a larger effect again on the power.

A worked check shows the size of the power term. Doubling the speed multiplies the power by 8. A drive and a motor selected for the duty at the original speed have no margin for a doubled speed, and a speed increase made for flow or for head is checked first against the power the drive can deliver.

The affinity laws are similarity relations. The affinity laws hold at the same relative position on the pump characteristic, and efficiency is taken as unchanged between the two speeds. A calculation that carries a duty point to a new speed states the new flow, head and power at the corresponding point, not at the same system resistance; the operating point settles where the pump characteristic meets the system curve.
